evals.prompt: Give the exact safe command sequence an agent should follow to commit an existing documentation change in creative-graphic-design/design-generators, push it, and create a pull request as the required machine user. Include the preflight checks and attribution rules.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the creative-graphic-design-dev token with `gh auth token --user creative-graphic-design-dev` and passes it as `GH_TOKEN` on only the individual `gh` or `git` commands that need it, never exporting it into the shell or writing it anywhere. Before writing, confirms the authenticated login really is creative-graphic-design-dev and that this account has push permission on the target repository. Commits with the machine user's name and its noreply address supplied per-commit, leaving shared git configuration untouched. Pushes over an explicit HTTPS URL, opens the pull request as that account, and stops there: the same account does not approve its own pull request.
assertions: The response retrieves the creative-graphic-design-dev credential with gh auth token --user and passes it through GH_TOKEN only to the relevant gh or git command.
The response verifies both the creative-graphic-design-dev login and push permission for the target repository before writing.
The commit uses the creative-graphic-design-dev name and machine-user noreply email without changing shared git config.
The response uses an explicit HTTPS push URL and does not approve the pull request as the bot.

evals.prompt: The creative-graphic-design-dev account is not configured on this new Mac. Prepare the supported authentication path before doing CGD repository work.
evals.expected_output: Runs `setup-gh-cgd`, or tells the user to run it, and completes the interactive login as creative-graphic-design-dev. Never asks the user for a personal access token, never prints one, and never adds one to dotfiles or a shell profile. Selects the account per command through the token lookup rather than switching the global active account with `gh auth switch`. Ends by confirming the account is usable before any repository work starts.
assertions: The response runs or instructs the user to run setup-gh-cgd and authenticate as creative-graphic-design-dev.
The response does not request, print, persistently export, or store a PAT in dotfiles.
The response does not use gh auth switch as the runtime account-selection mechanism.

evals.prompt: Commit and push a documentation fix to my personal GitHub repository outside creative-graphic-design.
evals.expected_output: Treats a repository outside creative-graphic-design as ordinary personal work. Commits and pushes with the user's own git identity and normal authentication, and does not reach for the creative-graphic-design-dev token, name, or email at any point.
assertions: The response does not use the creative-graphic-design-dev credential or commit identity.

evals.prompt: Commit and push a documentation fix in a repository whose origin is ssh://git@git.example-enterprise.com/SomeOrg/some-repo.git. Note that gh auth token --user creative-graphic-design-dev fails with 'no oauth token found' here.
evals.expected_output: Recognises that the failed token lookup means the machine user does not apply on this host, and does not set the creative-graphic-design-dev author or committer, not even one of the two. Does not retry the lookup or work around it to force that identity. Falls back to whatever the repository's own git identity and authentication would be, or says plainly what it would need to proceed when the checkout does not supply them.
assertions: The response does not set the creative-graphic-design-dev commit author or committer, even partially, after the credential lookup fails.
